title: Budapest Gambit: the ideas
line: Black gives a center pawn for quick play with the pieces, and usually wins it back.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Offer the pawn in front of your king. Black wants quick play for its pieces.

also.e7e6: That leads to the Nimzo-Indian or the Queen's Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the gambit.

steps.after: This is the Budapest Gambit. It is a risky choice that strong players rarely use.

steps.text: Jump the knight forward to attack the pawn on e5.
steps.after: White guards it with the bishop.

steps.text: Attack it again with the other knight.

steps.after: White blocks with the other knight.

steps.text: Bring the queen out. It attacks the pawn on e5 a third time.
steps.after: White pushes a pawn at the bishop.

steps.text: Take the pawn back with the knight from g4. Your bishop is attacked, but leave it: strong players take your knight here.
White slipped and took the bishop, a mistake club players often make. Find the checkmate with a knight.
steps.hint: Your queen pins the pawn in front of White's king, so it cannot take.
steps.after: The pawn in front of White's king cannot take the knight: your queen pins it.

summary: Black gives a center pawn, attacks it with both knights and the queen, and takes it back. One greedy capture loses.
